title: Workload capsule (capsule_bench_v0)
description: A compiler-input workload capsule: describes what to compile, the numeric golden policy, the expected Gemmini instruction coverage, the required oracle tiers, and the public/dev/hidden label. A capsule is an INPUT to the backend-under-test, never a kernel.

source_reference.description: bareMetalC path / torch module slice / ISA section / local spec id

dtype.description: Element type of this tensor. Not a fixed enum: the numeric-format vocabulary is data, declared in merlin/schemas/quant_formats.registry.yaml (where a new format -- MX, NVFP4, a GGUF k-quant -- is an entry, not a code change), so a list copied here goes stale the moment a target brings a format the list predates. Validity is enforced by merlin.targetgen.contract.schemas.validate_capsule against that registry plus plain machine accumulator widths, and an unknown token is still a hard ContractViolation.

op.description: The workload the capsule asks the backend to compile. Unlike dtype this IS a closed set, because an op is only expressible if the tooling can build its interface MLIR and produce its golden -- the vocabulary is code, not data. Its sources are merlin.targetgen.corpus_spec.BUILDERS (capsule + interface MLIR) and capsule_golden._recompute_golden (integer goldens; float ops carry an independent golden.yaml instead). Adding a builder without adding it here rejects the whole corpus at load, which is why merlin/tests/targetgen/test_capsule_vocabulary.py pins this list against BUILDERS.

dtype.description: Element type the golden comparison is performed in. Same open vocabulary as inputs[].dtype -- see that field.

instruction_classes.description: Required instruction classes, DERIVED per-target from the target's own ISA (e.g. gemmini RoCC classes, or a self-hosted ISA's semantic op patterns like MXUMatMul/TensorBaseOffset). Not a fixed enum: the class vocabulary is the target's, so validity is enforced by the per-target derivation (isa_taxonomy) + its coverage checker, not a hardcoded list here.

modes.description: Coverage axes this capsule exercises, as {mode: true}. Open for the same reason instruction_classes is: a mode names a datapath feature of the target under test, so the vocabulary belongs to the corpus and its target, not to this file. The closed list this replaced was gemmini's eight (i8/relu/acc_scale/k_accumulate/resident_reuse/conv2d/movement/padded_edge) and it rejected radiance's whole corpus over `rmsnorm: true`. coverage_report keeps those eight as the BASELINE always-reported axes so a 0 stays an explicit 'not covered' row, and unions in whatever else a corpus declares rather than dropping it.
